questions.question: After logout the app redirects to `/login` and the session cookie is gone. What best proves the session has really ended?
options: Check that the Log out button is no longer visible
Reload the login page and check its heading
Replay the old session cookie from a separate client and expect a `401`
Assert that `context.cookies()` returns an empty array
questions.explanation: The other checks only describe the browser. An app can clear the cookie while the server keeps the session alive, and only replaying the old cookie exposes that.

questions.question: An app keeps its access token in session storage. What happens if a test relies on `storageState()` alone?
options: The token is saved like local storage
The token is missing, so the next context starts signed out
Playwright throws an error when saving
The token is saved only with `indexedDB: true`
questions.explanation: `storageState()` saves cookies and local storage, plus IndexedDB on request, but never session storage. Copy that data yourself and restore it with `addInitScript()`.

questions.question: A project sets `use.storageState`. What does `browser.newContext()` with no options give you inside a test?
options: A signed-out context, because new contexts are always empty
An error, because the storage state is already in use
A context that shares cookies with the `page` fixture
A separate context that starts with the project's saved session
questions.explanation: Contexts created in a test inherit options from `use`, including `storageState`. Pass `storageState: { cookies: [], origins: [] }` to get a signed-out context.

questions.question: Why should the sign-in setup project use `trace: 'off'`?
options: Traces record the typed password and the session cookie
Tracing stops `storageState()` from saving
Setup projects can't record traces
Traces make the saved session expire sooner
questions.explanation: A trace holds action values, request bodies and cookies. Anyone who can open that artifact could read the credentials, even if they came from an environment variable.

questions.question: An app answers `/oauth/start` with a `302` to the identity provider. A test's `page.route()` on the provider's URL never runs. Why?
options: Routes can't match another origin
The glob needs a full regular expression
Routes don't run for requests that follow a server redirect
The route must be registered on the browser context
questions.explanation: Only the first request in a redirect chain reaches the route handler. Intercept the app's own start URL instead, then send the browser on to the callback.
